questions.stem: What mainly sets the changing thrust profile of a conventional solid rocket motor?
options: Continuous adjustment of liquid-propellant valves
The vehicle flight angle alone
The size of an emptied propellant tank after burnout
The exposed burning surface and propellant characteristics
questions.explanation: The grain geometry changes the exposed burning surface and therefore influences the thrust history.

questions.stem: Compared with many solid motors, what control can a suitable liquid rocket engine offer?
options: Changing propellant flow to adjust thrust
Reshaping the solid propellant grain during a burn
Guaranteeing immediate restart for every engine design
Removing the need to control the fuel-to-oxidizer mixture
questions.explanation: Suitable liquid engines can throttle by adjusting propellant flow; the capability depends on the engine design.

questions.stem: What is a characteristic of a cryogenic liquid propellant?
options: It must always ignite on contact with any other liquid
It must be stored at a very low temperature
It is necessarily a solid fuel-oxidizer mixture
It can always be stored near room temperature without insulation
questions.explanation: Cryogenic propellants are stored at very low temperatures, imposing tank and thermal-management requirements.

questions.stem: What does hypergolic mean for a propellant combination?
options: Both components must be stored as solids before mixing
Atmospheric oxygen is required for the mixture to ignite
The fuel and oxidizer ignite on contact
An external electric spark is always required for ignition
questions.explanation: A hypergolic fuel and oxidizer ignite spontaneously when brought into contact.

questions.stem: Why does a bipropellant chemical rocket carry an oxidizer for operation in space?
options: The oxidizer replaces the need to expel exhaust
The fuel can burn only when atmospheric oxygen is supplied
A rocket can obtain all oxidizer from the surrounding vacuum
There is no surrounding atmosphere to supply it
questions.explanation: A bipropellant rocket carries fuel and oxidizer, allowing it to operate without atmospheric oxygen.

questions.stem: Which property can make a suitable solid propellant useful for long-term storage?
options: It can remain stable for long periods under suitable storage conditions
It must remain cryogenic throughout storage
It is continuously pumped into the chamber during storage
It always burns spontaneously without ignition
questions.explanation: Suitable solid propellants can be stored for long periods, subject to their formulation and storage conditions.

questions.stem: What trade-off can recovery equipment impose on a launch stage?
options: Recovery removes the need to reserve propellant for landing
Its mass and recovery propellant can reduce payload capability
Recovery guarantees a lower cost for every mission
Recovery hardware never changes the available payload mass
questions.explanation: Recovery hardware and any reserved propellant add mass or reduce the resources available for payload delivery.

questions.stem: Why might a recovered engine still require work before reuse?
options: All components must be replaced after every flight regardless of condition
Inspection is unnecessary because flight cannot wear components
Thermal and mechanical loads can wear components
A landing restores consumed engine life automatically
questions.explanation: Thermal and mechanical loads can wear components, requiring inspection or refurbishment before reuse.

questions.stem: Why is thermal protection important for a returning launch vehicle?
options: Thermal protection is needed only while the vehicle is in deep vacuum
Thermal protection removes the need for trajectory control
Thermal protection eliminates all mechanical landing loads
Re-entry and atmospheric flight can produce high heating
questions.explanation: A returning vehicle can face significant aerodynamic heating, so its design must manage thermal loads.

questions.stem: What is one operational challenge of recovering a first stage far from its launch site?
options: Planning transport and recovery at the landing location
Eliminating the need to navigate toward the landing site
Making transport logistics independent of landing location
Avoiding all atmospheric loads during the return
questions.explanation: Recovery away from the launch site requires a suitable landing and retrieval plan.
